nodes.title: FFF1 device information response
nodes.summary: Observed 13-byte payload: 0B 01 1D 00 51 01 00 F7 00 00 00 00 00. The SDK independently documents IC_BB2 = 0x0B, but no explicit 13-byte FFF1 parser links this response to the SDK's icId field. Bytes 1-12 and byte 0's field role remain unverified.

nodes.title: FFF1 byte 0 may be the Realtek IC ID
nodes.summary: FFF1 byte 0 is observed as 0x0B, and the GloryFit SDK maps IC_BB2 to 0x0B and separately has an OTA icId field. No parser links FFF1 to that field, so this is a plausible but unverified interpretation; bytes 1-12 remain unknown.

nodes.title: Realtek SDK 0B -> BB2 mapping
nodes.summary: Verified from primary source in GloryFit v4.0.12 (APK pulled from the dedicated phone 2026-10-24 under owner authorization): classes5.dex embeds the RealSil SDK (com.realsil.sdk, Realtek's MCU brand) whose com.realsil.sdk.dfu.DfuConstants defines IC_BB2 = 0x0B alongside IC_BEE1/BBPRO/BEE2/BBLITE_ANC/BBPRO2/BBLITE/SBEE2/BBPRO3/BEE3 and MANUFACTURER_ID_REALTEK = 0x5D. BB2 is a vendor product-line label, not an RTL part number; the exact SoC remains unknown.

nodes.title: RealSil SDK GATT map matches observed T60 UUIDs
nodes.summary: The RealSil SDK in GloryFit v4.0.12 defaults its DFU GATT to service 0000d0ff-3c17-d293-8e48-14fe2e4da212 (exactly the observed T60 service) with characteristics 00006287/6387/6487 (same 128-bit base), MTU 256. Per-profile classes define 16-bit characteristics fff1/fff2 (and m.o pairs d0ff with fff3); ExtendedBluetoothDevice scans on fff6; classes6.dex defines services 55ff/56ff/57ff and characteristics fff0, ffd0-ffd5, ffd8. The observed 128-bit service 6a24eeab-4b65-4693-986b-3c26c352264f is the SDK's WELL_KNOWN_SPP_UUID (SPP transport). Observed 60FF/61FF services are absent from SDK string constants; their origin is unknown.

nodes.title: nRF Connect for Mobile is the phone's GATT client to T60
nodes.summary: Observed 2026-10-24 via read-only dumpsys bluetooth_manager on the dedicated phone (RFCNC10FA3K): Paul installed nRF Connect for Mobile (no.nordicsemi.android.mcp), which is the phone's current GATT client connected to the T60 (60:1A:B7:00:AE:67) since 10-24 22:34:42. Android's stack dump does not expose the remote GATT database, so the service tree and FFF1/FFF3 read values must be captured in the app or via a laptop GATT client (not installed).
